MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 6, 2023

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, September 6, 2023, in the Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams, the meeting
was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Carolyn Fowler
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aidé Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, ECD Director
  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Brian Espinoza, Planning Technician
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox, Planning Manager stated 1) Item 6A received one letter,
which was copied for the public to read as well as for each Planning
Commissioner.

Chairman Springs asked staff –
 Regarding the letter received for Item 6A, is it a letter
  requesting an extension from the applicant to the Planning
  Commission? Possibly stating they will not be able to attend?
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None.

(5) MINUTES:
Chairman Springs called for Minutes approval for the July 5, 2023
Planning Commission meeting and July 25, 2023, Special Planning
Commission Meeting.

MOTION:
Commissioner Trejo made the motion to approve the July 5, 2023
Planning Commission Minutes and seconded by Commissioner Shaw-
Williams.

Ayes:  Commissioners Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Abstained:  Commissioner Fowler.

Commissioner Fowler made the motion to approve the July 25, 2023
Special Planning Commission Minutes and seconded by Commissioner
Trejo.

Ayes:  Commissioners Fowler, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 6, 2023
(6) NON-PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A. ONE YEAR REVIEW OF SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-018 (SP-2019-
018) 3471 WEST CENTURY BOULEVARD: One Year Review of SP-2019-
018 approved on July 1, 2020, to allow the sale of distilled
spirits for off-site consumption from an existing retail store
on an approximately 11.8-acre, C-R (Commercial and Recreation)
zoned property at 3471 West Century Boulevard.

Ms. Wilcox made a brief staff presentation summarizing the staff
report.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff, there were none.

Chairman Springs asked staff –
 With the crime statistics from the Inglewood Police Department,
  he noticed there appears to me a rise in criminal activity and
  he asked staff if the rise is due in part not from the applicant
  but from the opening and continual attendance of the So-Fi
  Stadium attendees.
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Chairman Springs’ statement.

6B.  OVERVIEW,  CITYWIDE:  Overview  report  on  Micro-Unit
Regulations.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission, based upon the
criteria that was displayed by staff and further explained by Mr.
McCrumby, if there were any questions.

Chairman Springs asked staff –
 To further explain “by right” under the Overview.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

    Should micro-units be allowed as a by-right housing type?
    Should micro-unit developments require affordable units set
  aside?
    Should micro-units only be allowed within a half-mile of a
  Metro K and C Line Stations?
    Should the micro-units require parking?
    Should micro-units require Shared Amenity Space?

Commissioner Shaw-Williams –
 Concerned about the sizes of particular units, will the Planning
  Commission be able to set or require a condition to address unit
  sizes?
 What is the average rental rate for these micro-units?
 Agree that projects should be a half-mile of any of the Metro
  lines.
 Regarding parking – yes.
 Could you explain what is considered a Shared Amenity Space?
 Feels that it is a Yes to the Shared Amenity Space.
  - Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Shaw-Williams
  questions.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 6, 2023
Commissioner Trejo –
 What would the review process be for this type of development
  if there is no discretionary review?
 What if there is no laundry facilities in this type of
  development, would the planning commission at site plan review
  be able to impose a condition requiring laundry hook-ups if
  there is no laundry facility for a development?
 Believes that Inglewood is very quickly becoming not only an
  entertainment center, but also an employment hub, and that
  these types of developments might be great for service workers,
  i.e. servers for restaurants, not to mention the new hotel
  developments and the entertainment ventures that will need
  workers who will be able to live close.
 Will these developments receive an Environmental Review
  separate from the Site Plan Review process?
 Micro-Units by right – Yes, with certain standards.
 Micro-Units Require affordable units – Yes, at least 15
  percent.
 Micro-Units should be close to the Metro rail system, feels
  that these types of developments “should only be allowed” near
  the Metro Rail systems within one-half mile.
 Micro-Units require parking – Yes with one parking space as a
  requirement.
 Micro-Units should have Shared Amenity Space – Yes.
 I do have a wish list for these Micro-Units – I Would like to
  see added Bicycle Storage areas, area for packages to be
  received/delivered by Fed Ex, UPS along with the mail. Internet
  and, Appliances be included. I would like to have an Electric
  Charging Station.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.
   Ms. Wilcox responded to one of Commissioner Trejo’s
  question.

Commissioner Rice –
 A very real concern and feels that the Planning Commission
  should be involved in the entire complete process of these
  types of developments, and feels that the “by-right” is an
  easy switch by developers to state their project is a by-right
  development, submit their project and then will possibly
  attempt to over-saturate the area with micro-units.
 Should Micro-Units require affordable units – Yes, by at least
  20 percent.
 Should Micro-Units be close to the Metro rail system, Yes and
  only be allowed within the one-half mile.
 Should Micro-Units require parking – Yes, one parking space
  for every unit, but should the developer be allowed through
  the Micro-Unit development a density bonuses?
 Should Micro-Units have Shared Amenity Space – Yes.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.
   Mr. Jackson responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Fowler –
 Her concern is about over saturation of these types of
  developments and if having the “by-right” ability will be the
  cause.
 What would be the alternative if “Micro-Units by-right” is off
  the table?
 She stated she appreciates the full conversation, and how staff
  is attempting to get in front of this possible development
  action.

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 6, 2023

  Regarding Micro-Units requiring affordable units – Yes, in
  agreement with Commissioner Trejo at 50 percent. The major
  concern is the lack of quality materials that might be used,
  need to make sure that there is non-flammable materials and
  earthquake proof structures built, because if the Planning
  Commission is not allowed to properly oversee to make sure
  everything is done properly and with this area so near the
  earthquake fault-line it is another reason for concern.
  Should Micro-Units be required next to be within one-half mile
  of the Metrorail lines, definitely yes.
  Should Micro-Units require parking – Yes. Here in California
  it is necessary for vehicle use and especially if you have a
  child.
  Should Micro-Units require a Shared Amenity Space – Absolutely
  Yes.
  She stated that she spent multiple years in the state of
  California Housing area and it is vital that we have affordable
  housing for the residents here.

Chairman Springs
 Should micro-units be allowed as a by-right housing type – YES.
 Should micro-unit developments require affordable units set
  aside – Absolutely.
 Should micro-units only be allowed within a half-mile of a Metro
  K and C Line Stations – Absolutely YES.
 Should the micro-units require parking – YES Absolutely. Also
  feels that there should be parking spaces for Motorcycles as
  well.
 Should micro-units require Shared Amenity Space – YES.
 Now regarding laundry facilities on each of the floors, he
  believes that it might be difficult to demand that depending
  upon the size of the development, also regarding having hook-
  ups in each unit might be difficult.
 Tot-Lots, places for children activities, believes that should
  be implemented.
 He stated that these Micro-Units he feels are like the Bachelor
  Pads in the past, and the Lofts that are in the Downtown area
  of Los Angeles also.

Chairman Springs stated that each Planning Commissioner will have
:30 seconds to have closing remarks for tonight’s Overview.

Commissioner Fowler:
None.

Commissioner Rice:
 His major concern is that all of the previous projects that
  were approved by the Planning Commission recently, will want
  to return and demand that they resubmit their projects now as
  Micro-Units, in order to save money, time, and will not have
  to come before the Planning Commission due to “by-right”
  decision.
 Another concern is where staff remarked about one particular
  location that was approved for a specific number of units and
  now that project is applying for an even larger number of
  Micro-Units?

   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Rice’s remarks.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 6, 2023

Commissioner Trejo:
 Just wanted to say that she feels this is a great idea for
  Inglewood to be ahead of the State in what they may attempt to
  bring to the City to take away local control. This is good.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams:
 Since there is no requirement as to how many individuals can
  live in these types of Micro-Units, she feels that 50 percent
  seems to be a bit much, and feels better at 15 percent to 20
  percent max.

(7) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None.

(8) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:

Commissioner Fowler –
   Enjoyed going to the Ground Breaking for the 24hour EV
  Charging Station.
   Survived the Earthquake and Hurricane.
   Councilwoman Grey had a very nice Economic Town Hall at the
  Miracle Theater on Market Street. It was very well attended
  and wanted to thank Ms. Wilcox and Mr. Jackson who spoke and
  shared with the community, all of the upcoming projects.
   Los Angeles Business Journal Real Estate Event – which was a
  Planning Commission team trip to the Biltmore Hotel. Speakers
  did a great job especially sharing about the advancements and
  projects here in Inglewood, where we were in the past and how
  we are moving now in the present and what the future is going
  to look like and saw how my fellow colleagues were very happy
  to be from Inglewood.
   Was able to attend the Beyoncé Concert at Sofi, wonderful.
   National Voter Registration is on September 19, 2023 but in
  Inglewood, there will be a Voters Registration Event on the
  South-Lawn of City Hall on September 16, 2023 and looking
  forward to all coming out and attending.

Commissioner Rice –
   Everyone have a Great Weekend.

Commissioner Trejo –
   The clean-up of the un-housed on Century Boulevard under the
  405 Freeway has taken place and looks fantastic. There is
  also a Gas station on the corner of Century Boulevard and La
  Cienega that is adjacent to a cul-de-sac that was also cleaned
  up and I am not sure who did the cleaning, either Inglewood
  and/or Los Angeles but I want to commend them on a job very
  well done. For people who stay in the hotels near the Freeway,
  have to walk through those areas, and it smells poorly, and
  can be dangerous along with being very scary as well.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams –
   Stated she enjoyed the Los Angeles Business Journal event,
  really was wonderful.
   Her and her husband to join the new Iconix Gym in February
  2024.
   Everyone please have a great weekend, as her and her husband
  will be going to Alaska for Birthday Celebrations.

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 6, 2023
Chairman Springs –
   Thank you to everyone and staff, Planning Commission
  colleagues, for all of the cards and phone calls that he
  received on behalf of his family at the loss of his twin
  sister on August 23rd and her services will be this
  upcoming Monday, September 11th.

(9) ADJOURNMENT:
Chairman Springs closed this evenings Planning Commission Meeting
to be adjourned in Memory of his twin sister, Mrs. Loretta Springs
Broussard at 7:55 p.m.
